claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms multiple primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during conventional solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes a complex multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
The conventionally processed alloy has poor glass-forming ability and limited glass formation.
The proposed intervention is application of approximately 2 GPa external pressure during melt-spinning.
The proposed cooling rate is greater than 10^4 K/s.
The proposed reheating rate is below 20 K/min, with heating to approximately 1.1–1.2 Tg.
Applying high pressure to the undercooled liquid will reduce free volume.
Applying high pressure will restrict atomic mobility in the undercooled liquid.
Reduced free volume and restricted atomic mobility will raise the nucleation barrier for primary crystalline phases.
Approximately 2 GPa pressure will shift the alloy's liquidus and time–temperature–transformation curves.
The pressure-induced thermodynamic and kinetic changes will delay primary-phase nucleation during rapid cooling.
The intervention will minimize multistep crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Relative to processing without pressure, pressure-assisted melt-spinning will produce a significantly higher amorphous phase volume fraction.
The intervention will reduce the effective nucleation rate by at least 50%.
The intervention will shift crystallization onset to higher temperatures.
The intervention will improve the thermal stability of the glassy state.
Crystallization suppression is predicted to be effective only above a cooling rate of 10^4 K/s and with reheating below 20 K/min to about 1.1–1.2 Tg.
